text:
evan: Need a decision on how aggressive to be with Performance Lane pricing experiments. Two levers: lower baseline + higher surge, or higher baseline + smaller surge. Thoughts?

rita: Field note: enterprise buyers hate surprise surge bills. Prefer predictable baseline even if a bit pricier. SMBs prefer low baseline and pay-as-you-go.

noah: Finance modeling: lower baseline + high surge increases ARR volatility but can grow adoption. Higher baseline gives stable ARR. We can experiment with a feature flag for both in parallel.

tara: Ops concern: high-surge pattern spiky usage increases tail latency. We need clear throttling/priority rules and telemetry to measure queue impacts before wide rollout.

pricing-bot: Auto-scan: recommend A/B pilot with clear metrics: conversion rate, net revenue per seat, p95 latency delta, and churn risk. Logged experiment PR-4012.

evan: Proposal: run 8-week pilot with two SKUs: "Predictable" (higher baseline, softcap at baseline, low surge price) and "Elastic" (low baseline, 3x surge, prepaid burst discount). Track adoption by cohort.

rita: GTM ask: buyer kit for each SKU showing example TCO for three common workloads (chat, summarization, batch rerank). Also need messaging for procurement about surge caps.

noah: Billing note: make sure prepaid burst packs are available in both SKUs with identical conversion rates so experiments isolate baseline/surge preference.

ops-bot: Alert rule suggestion: if pilot causes >10% increase in p95 on shared pool for 15m, auto-disable Elastic SKU for that region.

tara: Agree. Also require canary deployment of entitlement system to validate throttling behavior.

evan: Action items: pricing-bot to publish experiment spec (due Mon), ops to add alert + canary (due Wed), noah to update billing conversion for parity (due Tue), rita to draft buyer kit outlines (due Thu). We'll review metrics at 4w and decide whether to extend or iterate.

rita: One more: include a clear line in T&Cs: "surge charges are itemized and capped per billing period" — helps procurement.

evan: Thanks all, will schedule sync Thu 10am PT. :rocket:
